The expression "a bridge too far" originated from Operation Market Garden during World War II. The phrase is ascribed to British General Frederick "Boy" Browning, who reportedly said it before the battle, and it was later recorded by historian Cornelius Ryan and popularized as the title of his 1974 book about the operation [d2][d8]. Some sources incorrectly claim the phrase was originated by Browning or coined by Ryan [d4][d5], but the credible historical account indicates it was a remark by Browning that Ryan used for his book's title [d2][d8]. The idiom now symbolizes an overly ambitious or unattainable goal [d1][d7][d9].
